description: We are Team ALPHA, a group of Semester 1 students participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We are interested in space exploration, technology, research and software development. Our proposed project, Forgotten Machines Atlas, aims to create an interactive educational platform that tells the stories of NASA equipment left on the Moon and Mars. We are here to learn, collaborate and build a meaningful solution using NASA's open resources.
summary:
Forgotten Machines Atlas is an interactive educational space museum developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, addressing the challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten."

Throughout the history of lunar and Martian exploration, numerous spacecraft, landers, rovers, scientific instruments and other equipment have been left behind or become inactive. Although these machines played important roles in space exploration, their stories are often overlooked.

Our project transforms this forgotten history into an immersive digital experience. Users can explore historical Moon and Mars equipment through interactive 3D models, static illustrations, detailed mission profiles, historical timelines, contextual audio and AI-assisted space history exploration.

The platform uses NASA's publicly available mission information and historical references to explain why these machines were sent, what they accomplished and what happened to them afterward.

Our goal is to make space history more accessible, engaging and memorable while preserving the scientific and historical legacy of humanity's exploration beyond Earth.
details:
Forgotten Machines Atlas — Project Details

1. What Does Our Project Do?

Forgotten Machines Atlas is an interactive digital space museum developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 under the challenge "Abandoned but not Forgotten: Storytelling about NASA's Discarded Equipment on the Moon and Mars."

During decades of space exploration, humanity has left behind numerous spacecraft, landers, rovers, scientific instruments and other equipment on the Moon and Mars. Many of these machines completed historic missions, but their stories are not widely known.

Our project aims to preserve and communicate these stories through an interactive educational platform where visitors can explore the machines, understand their missions and discover what happened to them after their operations ended.

2. How Does It Work? — Main Features

A. Interactive Moon and Mars Exploration

  • Separate exploration sections for the Moon and Mars.
  • Dedicated equipment profiles with historical information, mission descriptions and operational outcomes.
  • Exploration of different spacecraft and scientific equipment.

B. Interactive 3D and Static Models

  • Procedurally generated 3D planetary environments and equipment models.
  • Interactive 3D viewing to explore the shape and structure of historical machines.
  • Static illustration mode for an alternative visual experience.
  • Models are digital representations, not official NASA engineering models.

C. AI Space Historian

  • An AI-assisted conversational learning feature.
  • Visitors can ask questions about historical space missions and equipment.
  • Equipment-specific context helps users explore the history of selected machines.

D. AI Mission Comparison

  • Allows visitors to compare different historical missions and understand their differences, objectives and outcomes.

E. AI Knowledge Quiz

  • Interactive quiz experience that encourages visitors to test their understanding of space exploration history.

F. Historical Mission Timeline

  • Presents important mission events chronologically, helping visitors understand the development and history of space exploration.

G. Context-Aware Audio Experience

  • Background audio changes according to the section being explored, creating a more immersive museum experience.
  • Visitors can control the audio experience.

H. Search Atlas and Space Glossary

  • Search functionality to discover equipment and mission information.
  • A glossary to help visitors understand important space-science terminology.

3. NASA Data Sources and Their Use

The project uses publicly available NASA historical and mission information as its primary reference material.

Our main source is the NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA), which provides spacecraft records, mission parameters and historical information.

Additional NASA Science mission references were used to research individual equipment and missions.

Examples include:

  • Apollo Lunar Modules — NSSDCA
  • Lunar Roving Vehicles — NSSDCA
  • Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Packages (ALSEP) — NSSDCA
  • Surveyor missions — NASA Science
  • Mars Pathfinder and Sojourner — NASA Science
  • Spirit and Opportunity — NASA Science
  • Viking landers — NASA Science
  • Phoenix and InSight — NASA Science
  • Dawn spacecraft — NASA Science
  • NEAR Shoemaker — NASA Science
  • Pioneer 10 and 11 — NASA Science
  • Ingenuity Mars Helicopter — NASA Science
  • Kepler Space Telescope — NASA Science

Data implementation: Historical information is organized into structured local project data, including equipment-catalog.json and mission-timeline.json. These datasets provide the contextual information used by the website's equipment profiles, timelines and AI-assisted exploration features.

The platform uses curated project data based on NASA references rather than claiming to provide a live NASA database connection.

Official NASA resources:
https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/
https://science.nasa.gov/

4. Technologies and Software Used

The project was developed using a combination of web technologies, 3D graphics, AI tools and cloud deployment services.

Development and Programming

  • Google AI Studio — AI-assisted application development and prototyping.
  • React — Frontend user interface.
  • Vite — Development and build tooling.
  • JavaScript — Application functionality.
  • Tailwind CSS — Interface styling.
  • Three.js — Procedural 3D models and interactive planetary environments.
  • Node.js — Server-side runtime and application backend.

Artificial Intelligence

  • Google Gemini — AI-assisted space history exploration, mission comparison and knowledge quiz functionality.
  • Image generation tools — Creation of custom archival-style illustrations used in the website.

Design, Version Control and Deployment

  • GitHub — Source code repository and project version control.
  • Render — Website hosting and deployment.
  • HTML and CSS — Web interface structure and presentation.

5. Creativity and Innovation

The creative approach of Forgotten Machines Atlas is to transform historical mission information into an interactive museum experience instead of presenting it as ordinary articles or static information pages.

The project combines historical storytelling, procedural 3D visualization, contextual audio, structured mission information and AI-assisted learning in one platform.

An important aspect is that users can explore equipment visually, read about its mission, compare historical achievements and interact with an AI Space Historian.

The archival-style illustrations were generated specifically for this project and are artistic representations inspired by the real equipment and its historical environment. They are not original NASA photographs. Similarly, the 3D models are procedural digital representations created for educational visualization.

6. Benefits and Intended Impact

  • Makes historical space exploration more accessible to students and general audiences.
  • Encourages interest in astronomy, planetary science, engineering and space exploration.
  • Preserves awareness of important but less frequently discussed missions.
  • Makes complex historical information easier to understand through visual and interactive learning.
  • Encourages curiosity through AI-assisted questions, comparisons and quizzes.
  • Provides an educational platform that can be expanded with additional missions and equipment.

Our intended impact is to help people recognize that even when a spacecraft stops operating, its scientific contribution and historical importance remain.

7. Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered:

  • Historical accuracy and the importance of using reliable NASA references.
  • Clear differentiation between documented historical facts and AI-generated visual representations.
  • Accessibility of scientific information for learners with different levels of knowledge.
  • An engaging and consistent museum-style interface.
  • Interactive functionality rather than simply creating a static information website.
  • Performance and usability across different devices.
  • The possibility of expanding the platform with additional historical missions.

8. Future Scope

Forgotten Machines Atlas is an expandable educational project. Potential future improvements include:

  • Adding more forgotten spacecraft, landers, rovers and scientific instruments.
  • Expanding the 3D equipment collection with more detailed models.
  • Introducing additional NASA mission datasets and more structured historical records.
  • Improving AI responses with stronger source-grounded retrieval and references.
  • Adding multilingual educational content.
  • Improving accessibility and mobile responsiveness.
  • Introducing guided virtual museum tours and interactive educational activities.
  • Adding more detailed scientific information about the discoveries made by these missions.

Conclusion

Forgotten Machines Atlas is our effort to preserve the legacy of humanity's exploration of the Moon and Mars through technology, visualization and storytelling.

We believe that space exploration should not only be remembered through successful launches and active missions, but also through the machines that remain behind and the discoveries they made possible.

Their missions may have ended, but their stories continue.
